tasks.question: How does the workspace management interface ensure consistency when merging dependency graphs for locally developed packages into the consolidated dependency graph while preserving the original dependency relationships?
tasks.reference_answer: WorkspaceAPI.super_build_graph builds a new root, reuses non-editable nodes, and rejects cached nodes depending on editable nodes (conan/api/subapi/workspace.py:302-315). It records editable package options, skips editable-to-editable dependencies, and combines duplicate external requirements using aggregate before creating root edges (316-330). Requirement.aggregate merges flags and required_nodes (conan/internal/model/requires.py:235-265). This preserves the external dependency needs of collapsed packages, not every original edge or all graph metadata.

tasks.question: How can a revision tracking data structure that maintains a chronological list of version identifiers with timestamps be redesigned to provide thread-safe revision updates with atomic persistence across distributed server instances?
tasks.reference_answer: RevisionList is an in-memory list with JSON serialization (conans/server/revision_list.py:9-34), while ServerStore performs separate read and write operations (conans/server/store/server_store.py:161-171), each independently locked by the disk adapter (conans/server/store/disk_adapter.py:37-45). A redesign should make the entire read-modify-write a storage transaction keyed by recipe/package identity. For multiple servers, use a shared transactional store or an atomic compare-and-swap on a persisted version, retrying actual conflicts; local object locks alone are insufficient. Preserve duplicate-latest no-op behavior and chronological listing, and test concurrent additions/removals plus failure recovery. This is a proposed design, not an existing source guarantee.
